Article 21

Exemptions from proof of origin

1. Products sent as small packages from private persons to private persons or forming part of a traveller’s personal luggage shall be admitted as originating products without requiring the submission of a proof of origin, provided that such products are not imported by way of trade and have been declared as meeting the requirements of this Protocol and where there is no doubt as to the veracity of such a declaration. (a) for importation into the EU Party, 500 euros in the case of small packages or 1200 euros in the case of products forming part of a traveller’s personal luggage;

rows.task: Según el acuerdo UE-Corea, ¿hasta qué valor pueden entrar en Corea los pequeños paquetes sin prueba de origen? Dame también ese límite en euros con el tipo medio del BCE de octubre de 2026.
rows.note: Dorado q27 de la fase 3; 1.000 / 1,120159.
rows.final_answer:
The EU-Korea Free Trade Agreement allows small packages (value ≤ 1000 USD) entering Korea without origin proof, as per Article 21 of the Protocol on Origin. The equivalent value in euros as of October 2026 is **892.73 EUR** (based on the ECB's monthly average rate of 1.120159 USD/EUR). 

This limit is explicitly stated in the knowledge base (passage [3ac8ead017-0030]) and confirmed by the exchange rate tool. The EUR value reflects the BCE reference rate for that month. 

Final Answer:  
**Limit: 1000 USD (≈892.73 EUR)** under the EU-Korea agreement (Article 21, Protocol on Origin).

[EU-Korea Free Trade Agreement, Protocol concerning the definition of 'originating products' and methods of administrative cooperation: Protocol on origin, Titles I to VIII and Annex I (introductory notes) › TITLE V Proof of origin › Article 21 Exemptions from proof of origin]
Article 21

Exemptions from proof of origin

1. Products sent as small packages from private persons to private persons or forming part of a traveller’s personal luggage shall be admitted as originating products without requiring the submission of a proof of origin, provided that such products are not imported by way of trade and have been declared as meeting the requirements of this Protocol and where there is no doubt as to the veracity of such a declaration. In the case of products sent by post, this declaration may be made on a postal customs declaration or on a sheet of paper annexed to that document.

2. Imports which are occasional and consist solely of products for the personal use of the recipients or travellers or their families shall not be considered as imports by way of trade if it is evident from the nature and quantity of the products that no commercial purpose is intended.

3. Furthermore, the total value of these products shall not exceed:

(a) for importation into the EU Party, 500 euros in the case of small packages or 1200 euros in the case of products forming part of a traveller’s personal luggage;

(b) for importation into Korea, 1000 US dollars both in the case of small packages and in the case of the products forming part of a traveller’s personal luggage.

Exemptions from proof of origin

1. Products sent as small packages from private persons to private persons or forming part of a traveller’s personal luggage shall be admitted as originating products without requiring the submission of a proof of origin, provided that such products are not imported by way of trade and have been declared as meeting the requirements of this Protocol and where there is no doubt as to the veracity of such a declaration. Preservation of records

1. An exporter that has completed an origin declaration shall keep a copy of the origin declaration, as well as the supporting documents referred to in Article 25, for three years after the completion of the origin declaration or for a longer period of time as the Party of export may specify.
